mainTopic: Rules made מפני דרכי שלום, and the order of calling a כהן, a לוי and a ישראל to the תורה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משנה that lists rules made מפני דרכי שלום, for the sake of peace. These include filling the pit closest to the water channel first, not taking from someone's traps, not taking a find picked up by a חרש, שוטה or קטן, not taking olives a poor person knocked down, and letting poor gentiles take לקט, שכחה and פאה. The גמרא then asks for the source of the משנה's rule that a כהן reads from the תורה first and a לוי second, and four אמוראים each bring a פסוק. אביי asks why the משנה calls this rule 'for peace' if it comes from the תורה. The answer is that, unlike at a meal, in the בית הכנסת the כהן may not give his turn away to a greater person, because that could start fights. רב מתנה limits this to שבת and יום טוב, and רב הונא is shown to be a special case. אביי then teaches what happens when no כהן or no לוי is present. The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's rule against one כהן reading after another and against one לוי reading after another. The amud ends as the people of the גליל begin a question to רבי חלבו about who reads after the כהן and לוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The pit closest to the water channel gets filled first
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when one water channel feeds several pits, the pit nearest the channel fills first, to keep the peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pit that is closest to the water channel gets filled first, for the sake of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a set order for drawing water from a shared channel: the closest pit goes first. This is one item in a list of rules made מפני דרכי שלום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a fixed order, neighbors would fight over whose pit or field gets water first. The חכמים set a simple, clear rule, closest first, so there is nothing to argue about. The reason given is not ownership. It is keeping peace between people.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit or cistern that holds water
A water channel or irrigation ditch
Because of the ways of peace: a rule the חכמים made to prevent fights

phrases.english: A pit that is close to the water channel
phrases.notes: Here אמה means a water channel, not the measurement 'cubit.'

phrases.english: is filled first
because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹר שֶׁהוּא קָרוֹב לָאַמָּה מִתְמַלֵּא רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of rules made מפני דרכי שלום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pit nearest the channel is filled first, to prevent fights.

steps.title: Taking animals from someone else's traps
steps.stepSummary: Taking animals, birds or fish caught in another person's traps counts as גזל. The תנא קמא says this is because of דרכי שלום. רבי יוסי says it is full גזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animals, birds and fish caught in traps: taking them counts as robbery because of the ways of peace. רבי יוסי says: it is complete robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that you may not take animals out of another person's trap. It then records a disagreement about why: a rule for peace, or real robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trap's owner has not yet picked up the animals with his own hands. That is why the תנא קמא treats the ban as a peace rule made by the חכמים. רבי יוסי holds that taking them is גזל גמור, full robbery. Either way, taking them is forbidden. The two opinions argue only about how strong the ban is.

keyTerms.meaning: Traps or nets for catching animals
Robbery, taking what belongs to someone else

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree you may NOT take the animals. The disagreement is only whether this is גזל because of דרכי שלום (a rule of the חכמים) or גזל גמור (full robbery).

phrases.english: Traps for animals, birds, and fish,
phrases.notes: He means the animals already caught inside someone's traps.

phrases.english: there is in them a matter of robbery
because of the ways of peace;
Rabbi Yosei says: it is complete robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים, יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם גָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of דרכי שלום rules; adds the first case with רבי יוסי's disagreement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking trapped animals is גזל: because of דרכי שלום (תנא קמא), or full גזל (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: Taking a find from a חרש, שוטה, or קטן
steps.stepSummary: Taking a lost object that a חרש, שוטה or קטן picked up counts as גזל. The same disagreement appears between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A find picked up by a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor: taking it counts as robbery because of the ways of peace. רבי יוסי says: it is complete robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same pattern to a lost item found by someone who cannot formally acquire things. Again, taking it is forbidden, and רבי יוסי calls it full robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש, שוטה or קטן is not considered able to legally acquire an object by picking it up. So the תנא קמא again bases the ban on keeping the peace. רבי יוסי treats it as real robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: A found object, something that was lost
A minor, a child under bar/bas מצוה age

phrases.english: The find of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
there is in them a matter of robbery
because of the ways of peace;
Rabbi Yosei says: it is complete robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצִיאַת חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן, יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם גָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case following the same pattern as step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a find from a חרש, שוטה or קטן is גזל: because of דרכי שלום (תנא קמא), or full גזל (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: Olives under a poor person beating an olive tree
steps.stepSummary: When a poor person knocks olives off the top of a tree, taking the olives that fell beneath him counts as גזל. The same disagreement appears with רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A poor person who knocks olives off at the top of an olive tree: what is beneath him, taking it is robbery because of the ways of peace. רבי יוסי says: it is complete robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case in the same pattern: olives a poor person knocked down but has not picked up yet. Others may not grab them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor person has not taken hold of the fallen olives, so the תנא קמא again explains the ban as a peace rule. רבי יוסי says it is real robbery. Across all three cases, רבי יוסי consistently treats taking such things as גזל גמור.

keyTerms.meaning: Knocking or beating olives off the branches

steps.whatToRemember: In three cases (trapped animals, a find of a חרש שוטה וקטן, and olives knocked down by a poor person), the holder has not fully acquired the item, yet taking it is forbidden. The תנא קמא says it is גזל מפני דרכי שלום. רבי יוסי says it is גזל גמור.

phrases.english: A poor person who knocks olives off at the top of an olive tree,
what is beneath him is robbery
phrases.notes: He means the olives that fell to the ground under the tree.

phrases.english: because of the ways of peace;
Rabbi Yosei says: it is complete robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָנִי הַמְנַקֵּף בְּרֹאשׁ הַזַּיִת, מַה שֶּׁתַּחְתָּיו גָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third parallel case completing the series with רבי יוסי's disagreement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking olives beneath a poor person beating a tree is גזל: because of דרכי שלום (תנא קמא), or full גזל (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: Poor gentiles may take gifts for the poor, for the sake of peace
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that we do not stop poor gentiles from taking לקט, שכחה and פאה, because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not protest when poor gentiles take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last example of a rule made to keep the peace: poor gentiles are allowed to take the gifts that the תורה gives to the poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the תורה, לקט, שכחה and פאה are meant for Jewish poor people. Still, חז״ל said we should not chase poor gentiles away from them, so that relations stay peaceful. This rule belongs to the same list as the earlier steps, where a rule is based on keeping the peace.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not protest or stop them
Stalks that fall during harvesting and are left for the poor
Sheaves forgotten in the field, which are left for the poor
The corner of the field, left unharvested for the poor

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of rules made for דרכי שלום ends here: watering pits in order, traps, finds of a חרש שוטה וקטן, the olives a poor person knocks down, and poor gentiles taking gifts meant for the poor.

phrases.english: We do not protest against poor gentiles
who take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last case to the משנה's list of rules based on keeping the peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poor gentiles are not stopped from taking לקט, שכחה and פאה, for the sake of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן reads first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn the משנה's rule that a כהן reads from the תורה first, then a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: From where do we learn these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a question. This sets up the next steps, where four אמוראים each give a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not point to the last line we just learned. It goes back to the very first rule of the משנה: at a public תורה reading, a כהן goes first, then a לוי, then a ישראל. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק this order is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
From where do we learn these things? (a request for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't connect this question to the poor gentiles we just learned about. The גמרא is going back to the opening rule of the משנה, that a כהן is called to the תורה first and a לוי second.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where are these things learned?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the start of the משנה: a כהן reads first, then a לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of דרכי שלום rules and goes back to the משנה's first rule to look for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that a כהן reads from the תורה before a לוי?

steps.title: רב מתנה: משה gave the תורה to the כהנים, sons of לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה brings the פסוק where משה gives the תורה to 'the כהנים, sons of לוי.' The extra words teach the order: כהן first, then לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: The פסוק says, 'And משה wrote this תורה and gave it to the כהנים, the sons of לוי.' Don't I already know that the כהנים are sons of לוי? Rather, it teaches: a כהן first, and afterward a לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers the question with a פסוק and shows how its extra wording teaches the order of who is called to the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows the כהנים come from the tribe of לוי, so the words 'sons of לוי' seem to add nothing. רב מתנה reads them as naming two groups in order: first the כהנים, then the rest of לוי. Since this פסוק is about handing over the תורה, it fits the order of תורה reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces an obvious point the פסוק would not need to tell us)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way of reading a פסוק: when it seems to say something obvious, the extra words must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said: As the verse says:
"And Moshe wrote this Torah
and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi"
Is that to say I don't know
that the priests are the sons of Levi?
Rather, it means a priest first,
and afterward a Levite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'sons of לוי' in דברים לא:ט teach the order: כהנים first, then the rest of לוי.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: The כהנים, sons of לוי, shall come near
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא brings a different פסוק with the same extra words, 'the כהנים, sons of לוי,' and learns the same order from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: From here: 'And the כהנים, the sons of לוי, shall come near.' Don't we already know that the כהנים are sons of לוי? Rather, it teaches: a כהן first, and afterward a לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another source for the same rule, using the same kind of reasoning about extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as רב מתנה's: the obvious-seeming 'sons of לוי' is read as setting an order. Only the פסוק is different. This one is about the כהנים coming forward to serve, and not about receiving the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The smith (a nickname of רבי יצחק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said: From here:
"And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come near"
Is that to say we don't know
that the priests are the sons of Levi?
Rather, it means a priest first,
and afterward a Levite.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same rule, using the same reasoning as רב מתנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'sons of לוי' in דברים כא:ה teach the order: כהן first, then לוי.

steps.title: רב אשי: אהרן was set apart as holy of holies
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a פסוק from דברי הימים saying that אהרן was set apart to be especially holy. This shows that the כהנים rank above the rest of לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: From here: 'The sons of עמרם were אהרן and משה; and אהרן was set apart, to be sanctified as most holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives a source that works in a different way. It does not rely on extra words. It relies on a פסוק that directly says אהרן was made holier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה and אהרן were both sons of עמרם from the tribe of לוי. Still, only אהרן and his descendants were set apart as 'holy of holies.' So the כהנים have a higher level of holiness than other לויים, and that is why they are called to the תורה first.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of משה and אהרן

steps.whatToRemember: So far, three sources for 'a כהן reads first, then a לוי': (1) רב מתנה, from 'the כהנים, sons of לוי' when משה gave over the תורה; (2) רבי יצחק נפחא, from 'the כהנים, sons of לוי shall come near'; (3) רב אשי, from 'אהרן was set apart as holy of holies.' The next step adds a fourth source from רבי חייא בר אבא.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: From here:
"The sons of Amram: Aharon and Moshe,
and Aharon was set apart
to be sanctified as most holy."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third source, based on a different kind of proof: the holiness of אהרן, not extra wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אהרן, and through him the כהנים, was set apart with greater holiness than the rest of לוי, so the כהן goes first.

steps.title: A fourth source: 'And you shall sanctify him'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא learns the כהן's priority from the פסוק 'וקדשתו', which gives the כהן first place in every matter of holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: we learn it from here: 'And you shall sanctify him' means treating the כהן as holy in every matter of holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more answer to its question of where we learn that a כהן reads first. רבי חייא בר אבא points to the פסוק 'וקדשתו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers used 'כהנים בני לוי' and the פסוק about אהרן being set apart. This answer uses a general command to honor the כהן. Reading from the תורה is a 'matter of holiness', so the כהן goes first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall sanctify him': a command to treat the כהן as holy
A matter of holiness, such as Torah, ברכות and holy things

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: from here:
"And you shall sanctify him"
for every matter of holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source for the same rule, after רב מתנה, רבי יצחק נפחא and רב אשי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a כהן reading first
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וקדשתו': the כהן comes first in every matter of holiness.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל spells out 'every matter of holiness'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל reads 'וקדשתו' the same way and lists examples: the כהן opens first, blesses first and takes a fine portion first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And you shall sanctify him' means in every matter of holiness: to open first, to say the blessing first, and to take a nice portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי חייא בר אבא's reading of 'וקדשתו' and gives concrete examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the reading of 'וקדשתו' is an old teaching and not only רבי חייא's idea. The examples (opening first, leading the blessing, choosing a nice portion) show how far the כהן's honor reaches. Reading the תורה first fits the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: 'וקדשתו' gives the כהן first place in all matters of holiness: speaking first, blessing first, and choosing a portion first.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"And you shall sanctify him": for every matter of holiness;
to open first,
phrases.notes: He means being the first to speak when people gather to learn.

phrases.english: and to bless first,
and to take a fine portion first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and spells out רבי חייא בר אבא's reading.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of 'וקדשתו' as covering every matter of holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: If it is a Torah law, why call it 'for the sake of peace'?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף: the משנה says the כהן reads first מפני דרכי שלום, but we just saw that it is a Torah law!
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: 'Because of the ways of peace'?! It is from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the wording of the משנה. If the פסוקים teach that a כהן goes first, why does the משנה give 'peace' as the reason?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מפני דרכי שלום usually describes a rule the חכמים made to keep peace. But the גמרא just brought several פסוקים showing this rule comes from the Torah. So the reason the משנה gives seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the ways of peace: to keep peace between people

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not questioning that the כהן reads first. He is only asking why the משנה gives 'peace' as the reason.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
"Because of the ways of peace"?!
It is from the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the Torah sources just brought to question the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's reason 'מפני דרכי שלום' for the כהן reading first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule with a Torah source should not need a rabbinic-style reason like keeping peace.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is both Torah law and for peace
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the rule comes from the Torah, and its purpose is peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is from the Torah, and it is because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by saying there is no conflict: the Torah made this rule, and the reason behind it is peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יוסף's view, the משנה is not calling this a rabbinic rule. It is only telling us why the Torah set this order: so people will not fight over who reads first.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is from the Torah, and it is because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּמִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the phrase as the purpose of the Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מפני דרכי שלום' means the rule is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is from the Torah, and peace is its purpose.

steps.title: But the whole Torah is for peace
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rejected: every law in the Torah is for peace, so saying it here tells us nothing special.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole Torah is also for the sake of peace, as it is written: 'Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's answer, using a פסוק in משלי that says the whole Torah is about peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If peace is the purpose of every Torah law, there is no reason for the משנה to name it for this rule alone. So רב יוסף's answer does not explain why the משנה used these words here.

phrases.english: The entire Torah, too,
is because of the ways of peace,
as it is written: "Her ways are ways of pleasantness
and all her paths are peace"!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ נָמֵי מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down רב יוסף's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the rule is from the Torah and for peace
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole Torah is for peace, naming peace for this one law adds nothing.

steps.title: אביי: it goes beyond the meal rule, where honor may be given away
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer that connects the משנה to a ברייתא about eating together. At a meal, the person who breaks the bread eats first but may hand that honor to his teacher or someone greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: it is like מר's teaching. As it was taught: Two people eating from one dish wait for each other. Three do not wait. The one who breaks the bread reaches in first, but if he wants to give honor to his teacher or to someone greater than him, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: After רב יוסף's answer fails, אביי offers his own answer. He brings a ברייתא about table manners as background.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that at a meal, the person who has the right to go first may give that right to someone greater. The usual explanation of אביי is that the משנה's 'מפני דרכי שלום' teaches something extra about Torah reading. There the כהן reads first even before a greater scholar, and the order may not be changed, so that people will not fight.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with what my master taught
The one who breaks the bread
He is allowed (it is up to him)

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן reading first is a Torah law. The משנה adds 'מפני דרכי שלום' to show that this order is fixed. At a meal, the first person may give his place to someone greater; with Torah reading, the order stays the same so there is no fighting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a כהן is called up first even when a great תלמיד חכם is present.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said: it is in line with what Mar taught;
phrases.notes: 'מר' means 'master.' אביי is referring to his teacher.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: שְׁנַיִם – מַמְתִּינִין זֶה לָזֶה בַּקְּעָרָה.
phrases.english: as it was taught: two people wait for each other at the dish.
Three do not wait.
The one who breaks the bread stretches out his hand first,
but if he wants to show honor
to his teacher or to someone greater than him,
he is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְכִדְמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's failed answer with a new explanation of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the phrase a new, specific meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מפני דרכי שלום' is just the general purpose of a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase teaches something extra beyond the meal rule, where the first person may give his honor to someone greater.

steps.title: Giving away the honor works at a meal, but not in the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ברייתא's permission to hand the first portion to a greater person applies only at a meal. In the בית הכנסת it is not allowed, because it would lead to fights.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master said about that ברייתא: This was only taught about a meal. But in the synagogue, no, because people will come to quarrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer from step 15. It explains that the 'peace' reason in the משנה means the כהן may not give away his turn in the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a meal, a person may give his honor of going first to his רבי. In the בית הכנסת this is forbidden, because people would start arguing over who is the most important. So 'מפני דרכי שלום' does tell us something new: even if the כהן wants to give up his turn, he may not, so that peace is kept.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about (a limiting phrase)

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן's first עליה is from the Torah. The words 'מפני דרכי שלום' add that in the בית הכנסת he may not give that honor away, even to someone greater, so that no fights break out.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'peace' is the reason the כהן goes first. The Torah already gave him that right. The 'peace' reason explains why he cannot hand his turn to someone else in shul.

phrases.english: And the Master said about it:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is רבה, and 'it' is the ברייתא about eating together from step 15.

phrases.english: They only taught this about a meal,
but in the synagogue, no,
because they will come to quarrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר עֲלַהּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּסְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer by adding רבה's limiting statement on the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what 'מפני דרכי שלום' adds: it does not explain why the כהן goes first. It forbids him from giving away his turn in the בית הכנסת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מפני דרכי שלום' seemed to say nothing new, since all of Torah is for peace.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that, unlike at a meal, in the בית הכנסת the כהן may not give his honor to someone greater, because that would cause fights.

steps.title: The ban applies only on שבת and יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה limits the rule: the כהן may not give away his turn only on שבת and יום טוב, when many people come. On Monday and Thursday he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: What you said, that in the synagogue it is not allowed, we only said on שבת and יום טוב, when many people are there. But on Monday and Thursday, the ban does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה narrows the rule from the last step. The worry about fights is only when big crowds come to shul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban is fear of quarrels, and quarrels happen when there is a big crowd. On Monday and Thursday few people come, so there is less to worry about. On those days a כהן may let a greater person read first.

keyTerms.meaning: Monday and Thursday, the weekday Torah reading days

phrases.english: רב מתנה said:
This that you said, 'in the synagogue, no,'

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיָמִים טוֹבִים –
phrases.english: we only said it about Shabbatot and Yamim Tovim,
when many people are present,
but on Monday and Thursday, no.
phrases.notes: He means the ban does not apply then, so the כהן may give his turn to someone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת לֹא, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבה's rule to the days when crowds are present.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the בית הכנסת the כהן may not give his first עליה to someone else on שבת and יום טוב, but on Monday and Thursday he may.

steps.title: But רב הונא read first even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: רב הונא, who was not a כהן, read the כהן's portion even on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב הונא would read the כהנים' portion on שבת and יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule with a story. A great non-כהן read first on the very days רב מתנה said it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to steps 16-17, on שבת and יום טוב a כהן may not give his turn to someone else. But רב הונא, a ישראל, read first on exactly those days. This seems to go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He read the portion of the כהנים, the first עליה

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But רב הונא would read the portion of the כהנים
on Shabbatot and Yom Tov!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב הוּנָא קָרֵי בְּכָהֲנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of steps 16-17 from what רב הונא actually did.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a כהן may not give his first עליה to someone else on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא, a non-כהן, read first on שבת and יום טוב, which should be forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא was different because everyone accepted his greatness
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא was a special case: even רבי אמי and רבי אסי, the leading כהנים of ארץ ישראל, accepted his authority, so no one would fight about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא is different, because even רבי אמי and רבי אסי, the important כהנים of ארץ ישראל, would bow to his authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב הונא was an exception, not a contradiction to the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban exists because people might fight over who is greatest. With רב הונא there was nothing to fight about, since even the greatest כהנים accepted that he was above them. Since there was no risk of a quarrel, the reason for the ban did not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: They would bow to him, accepting his authority

phrases.english: רב הונא is different,
for even רבי אמי and רבי אסי,
the important כהנים of ארץ ישראל,
would bow to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by showing רב הונא was a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the case an exception: the reason for the rule (fear of quarrels) did not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's practice seemed to show that a non-כהן may read first on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. רב הונא was allowed only because his greatness was accepted by all, even the leading כהנים, so no fight could arise.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on giving away the first עליה is about avoiding fights. When someone's greatness is accepted by everyone, as with רב הונא, the worry is gone.

steps.title: With no כהן, the לוי loses his special place
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a tradition: if there is no כהן in shul, the fixed order is broken, and a לוי does not automatically get the first עליה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that if there is no כהן there, the bundle is taken apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic about the order of עליות. אביי shares a tradition about what to do when no כהן is present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order כהן, then לוי, then ישראל is like one tied bundle. If the כהן is missing, the bundle comes apart. The לוי no longer gets a set place ahead of ישראלים.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition, we hold
The bundle is taken apart: the fixed order is broken

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the לוי can never read first. It means he has no special right to go before the ישראלים when there is no כהן.

phrases.english: אביי said: We have a tradition:
if there is no כהן there,
the bundle is taken apart.
phrases.notes: The 'bundle' is the set order of כהן, then לוי. Without the כהן, the לוי loses his special turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, נָקְטִינַן: אֵין שָׁם כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what to do when one of the groups in the order is missing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no כהן is present, the fixed order breaks, and a לוי has no set right to go before ישראלים.

steps.title: With no לוי, the כהן reads again
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a second tradition: if there is no לוי, the כהן reads the לוי's portion too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: We have a tradition that if there is no לוי there, a כהן reads.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second tradition about a missing group. Here the לוי is missing, and the כהן fills his place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite case from step 20. When the לוי is missing, the second עליה does not go to a ישראל. The same כהן who read first reads again in the לוי's place.

keyTerms.meaning: A member of the tribe of Levi, who gets the second עליה

steps.whatToRemember: No כהן: the order breaks, and the לוי has no special place. No לוי: the כהן reads again in his place.

phrases.english: And אביי said: We have a tradition:
if there is no לוי there, a כהן reads.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי, נָקְטִינַן: אֵין שָׁם לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second tradition of אביי, covering the case of a missing לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no לוי is present, a כהן reads the לוי's portion.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says one כהן should not read after another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's rule that a כהן reads in place of a missing לוי, using רבי יוחנן's rule that a כהן should not read after a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יוחנן said: a כהן should not read after a כהן, because people will think something is wrong with the first one. A לוי should not read after a לוי, because people will think something is wrong with both of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's tradition from Step 21. If a כהן reads the לוי's portion, it looks like a כהן reading after a כהן, which רבי יוחנן forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן worries that calling a second כהן makes people think the first one was found not to be a real כהן. For two לויים, people might doubt either one. So how can a כהן take the לוי's place?

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw or blemish, here a doubt about someone's family status
The flaw of the first one
The flaw of both of them

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
A כהן should not read after a כהן,
because of the flaw of the first one.
phrases.notes: People might think the first man turned out not to be a real כהן, so another was called to replace him.

phrases.english: A לוי should not read after a לוי
because of the flaw of both of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's second tradition from Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that a כהן reads the לוי's portion when no לוי is present
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן reading after a כהן is forbidden by רבי יוחנן because it casts doubt on the first כהן.

steps.title: The same כהן reads again
steps.stepSummary: אביי's rule means the same כהן who already read also reads the לוי's portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we said a כהן reads in place of the לוי, we meant the same כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. No new כהן is called; the first כהן simply reads a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's worry only applies when a different כהן comes up after the first. If the same man reads again, nobody will think the first כהן was replaced, so there is no doubt about anyone's status.
steps.whatToRemember: With no לוי, the same כהן reads twice. A different כהן is not called up after the first.

phrases.english: When we said it,
we meant the same כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמְרִינַן, בְּאוֹתוֹ כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A different כהן would read the לוי's portion, which clashes with רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: The same כהן reads again, so there is no doubt about anyone

steps.title: Why are two כהנים different from two לויים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן worries about both people with two לויים, but only about the first with two כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a לוי after a לוי, where both are doubted? People say one of them is not a לוי. With a כהן after a כהן too, people would say one of them is not a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's own statement. It wants to know why the two cases are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two לויים, people suspect that one of them, either the first or the second, is not a real לוי. The same logic should apply to two כהנים: the second one might be the fake. So why does רבי יוחנן worry only about the first כהן?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are not treated alike)

phrases.english: What is different about a לוי after a לוי,
that there is a flaw for both of them?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ לָאו לֵוִי הוּא;
phrases.english: Because people say: one of them is not a לוי.
With a כהן after a כהן too,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ לָאו כֹּהֵן הוּא!
phrases.english: people would say: one of them is not a כהן!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא לֵוִי אַחַר לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending אביי to questioning רבי יוחנן's distinction
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's distinction between two כהנים and two לויים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The suspicion that one of the two is fake applies equally to both cases.

steps.title: The second כהן's father is a known כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is talking about a case where everyone knows the second כהן's father is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where we know for sure that the father of this second one is a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by describing the case. The second כהן comes from a known כהן family, so no one doubts him, and only the first is suspected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the second man's father is a known כהן, people will not suspect him. The only person left to doubt is the first כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a firm presumption, it is well known to us

phrases.english: It is a case where we have a firm presumption
about the father of this second one,
that he is a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן דְּמוּחְזָק לַן בַּאֲבוּהּ דְּהַאי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24
steps.terutzMaskana: The second כהן's lineage is known, so only the first is doubted

steps.title: The same could be said of the second לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: say the same about לויים, where the second one's father is a known לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, let it be a case where we know that the father of the second one is a לוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 25. If a known father protects the second כהן, a known father should protect the second לוי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If that were true, the second לוי would also be safe from suspicion, and only the first לוי would be doubted. So why does רבי יוחנן say both לויים are doubted?

phrases.english: Here too,
let it be where we have a presumption about the father of this second one,
that he is a לוי!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, דְּמוּחְזָק לַן בַּאֲבוּהּ דְּהַאי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a known father protects the second person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same protection should apply to the second לוי, which would cancel the doubt about both לויים.

steps.title: People suspect the לוי's father married someone forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Even if the father is a known לוי, people might say he married a ממזרת or a נתינה, so his son is not a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, people say: he married a ממזרת or a נתינה and disqualified his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second לוי is still doubted. A known father is not enough, because the mother might have made the children lose their status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a לוי marries a ממזרת or a נתינה, the children lose their לוי status. So even with a known לוי father, people can suspect that the second man is not a real לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden relationship
A woman from the גבעונים, who were not allowed to marry into the Jewish people

phrases.english: Rather, people say:
He married a ממזרת or a נתינה,
and disqualified his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמְרִי: מַמְזֶרֶת אוֹ נְתִינָה נְסֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 26
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A known לוי father removes all doubt about the son
steps.terutzMaskana: People can still suspect the mother disqualified the children

steps.title: The same could be said of the כהן's father
steps.stepSummary: Then people could also say the second כהן's father married a גרושה or a חלוצה and made his children חללים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, people could say: he married a divorced woman or a חלוצה and made his children חללים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new answer back onto the כהנים. If a forbidden marriage can ruin a לוי's son, it can ruin a כהן's son too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who marries a גרושה or a חלוצה has children who are חללים, without כהונה. So the second כהן should also be suspected, and the difference between the two cases seems to disappear again.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman, forbidden to a כהן
A woman released from יבום by חליצה, also forbidden to a כהן
He made his children חללים (without כהונה)

phrases.english: Here too, people would say:
He married a divorced woman or a חלוצה,
and made his children lose their כהונה!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, אָמְרִי: גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ חֲלוּצָה נְסֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only the second לוי, not the second כהן, can be suspected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forbidden marriage can strip a כהן's son of כהונה just as it strips a לוי's son of his status.

steps.title: A disqualified כהן is still never a לוי
steps.stepSummary: Even if the second כהן lost his כהונה, he would become a ישראל, not a לוי. So he could not be reading in the לוי's place.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, does he become a לוי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer that settles the difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son who loses his כהונה becomes a plain ישראל, never a לוי. So calling the second man after a כהן would make no sense on any explanation, unless he really is a כהן. People will not doubt him, only the first כהן. With two לויים, the second can be suspected of being a ישראל, so both are doubted.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן after a כהן: only the first is doubted, because a disqualified second כהן would be a ישראל, not a לוי. A לוי after a לוי: both are doubted.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer is a rhetorical question. "Does he become a לוי?!" means "Of course not, he would just be a ישראל."

phrases.english: In the end,
does he become a לוי?!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, לֵוִי מִי קָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 28 and closes the question of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the suspicion does not fit the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A disqualified second כהן could be suspected just like a second לוי
steps.terutzMaskana: A disqualified כהן becomes a ישראל, never a לוי, so the second כהן is not doubted

steps.title: Who would actually suspect the first כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who might wrongly think the first כהן is disqualified, and rules out the people who stay until the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are we worried about? If it is the people sitting there, they see that he was counted as one of the readers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks exactly whose wrong idea we are worried about. It tests the first option, the people who stay in the בית כנסת, and shows they would not be fooled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that people would say the first כהן is a חלל, because a second כהן was called after him. But people who stay to the end see that the first כהן was counted as one of the seven readers, so they know he is a proper כהן. That means the worry cannot be about them.

keyTerms.meaning: And for whom? (whose mistake are we worried about)
Those sitting (people who stay in the בית כנסת until the end)
But they see him (they see what really happened)

phrases.english: And for whom (is there a worry)?
phrases.notes: He means: who would think the first כהן is not a real כהן?

phrases.english: If for those sitting there,
but they see him!
phrases.notes: They see he was counted as one of the seven readers, so they know he is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן? אִי לְיוֹשְׁבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling why a לוי or second כהן causes the worry, the גמרא now asks who the worry is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which group of people would wrongly suspect the first כהן's lineage.

steps.title: The worry is about people who leave early
steps.stepSummary: The worry is about people who walk out before the קריאת התורה ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the worry is about the people who leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the worry is about people who leave the בית כנסת early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who walk out only see a second כהן being called after the first one. They never see that the first כהן was counted among the seven readers, so they might think he was a חלל. That is why a second כהן should not be called after the first.

keyTerms.meaning: Those leaving (people who go out before the end)

steps.whatToRemember: The worry about calling a second כהן is only because of people who leave early and miss the full picture.

phrases.english: Rather, for those who leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְיוֹצְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 after ruling out the people who stay.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is for people who leave before the reading ends and do not see that the first כהן was counted.

steps.title: The people of the גליל send a question to רבי חלבו
steps.stepSummary: A new question begins: the people of the גליל ask רבי חלבו about who reads after the כהן and the לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of the גליל sent a question to רבי חלבו: After them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. It is setting up a question that the people of the גליל sent to רבי חלבו, and the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "After them" means after the כהן and the לוי who read first. The question will ask who should be called up next. The rest of the question comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a question sent by message)
After them (after the כהן and the לוי)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי גָלִילָא לְרַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ:
phrases.english: The people of the Galilee sent to Rabbi Ḥelbo:
After them,

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי גָלִילָא לְרַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the order of readers after the כהן and לוי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is called to read after the כהן and the לוי (the question continues on the next amud).
